title: Dynamics 365 Business Central Blog Series: Integrate with Microsoft Dataverse
summary: The post outlines three methods to integrate Business Central with Microsoft Dataverse: using the standard Dataverse connector with job queue-based synchronization, using integration tables (CDS TableType), or calling Dataverse APIs directly. It covers setup procedures, OAuth authentication, custom table integration, and recent enhancements across multiple releases.
key_points: Three integration approaches exist: standard connector (scheduled sync), integration tables (CDS TableType), and direct Dataverse API calls
Standard Dataverse connector uses scheduled job queue entries and does not guarantee real-time data consistency
OAuth 2.0 with Client Credentials grant type can authenticate Dataverse API calls via tools like Postman
Recent features enable mapping new Dataverse fields, using synthetic relationships, safe company copying with integration, and multi-currency support
Integration table mappings can be customized and extended for both standard and custom Dataverse tables

quotes.text: Using OAuth 2.0 to connect Dataverse tables (APIs) in Postman (Using Grant type: Client Credentials, not Implicit)
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies the correct OAuth grant type for API-based Dataverse integration, guiding developers on proper authentication setup

quotes.text: New and custom Dataverse tables are readily available for mapping from the lookup on Integration Table column.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the evolution toward easier integration setup by making custom and new tables immediately available for mapping without manual configuration
